title: Paris Sets Night Curfews After Weekend Protests
summary:
Police in Paris, France, set a night curfew on Monday in two parts of the city. A curfew is a rule that says people must stay off certain streets at certain hours.

The curfew came after big protests across France on Saturday. People were upset about rising prices and poor conditions in schools. Most protests in France are peaceful, but some people turned violent and damaged buildings and stores. Officials said at least 3,000 businesses were damaged, and at least 2,400 people were arrested.

In Paris, the curfew covered a big square and a shopping area from 11 p.m. Monday to 6 a.m. Tuesday. Some cities, including Lille and Nice, set curfews for kids and teens under 18.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said no one was killed. President Emmanuel Macron asked leaders to explain what went wrong in planning and to find new ways to stop the violence.
why_it_matters: It shows how people can speak up about things like schools, and how leaders try to keep everyone safe.
